newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan ups military force in Damazin - travellers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan ups military force in Damazin - travellers.

text.p: Sudan is increasing its military and air presence in the strategic southeastern town of Damazin to counter any attacks by rebel forces, travellers returning from the area said on Wednesday.
They said Sudanese soldiers, some with machineguns slung over their shoulders, were more visible on the streets of the town where government troops are massing for a counterattack.

On the eight-hour journey to Khartoum, travellers saw convoys of military vehicles packed with food supplies heading in the opposite direction towards the southern town but said there were few troop transport vehicles that day.
There were more checkpoints than normal, about eight compared to half that many before the fighting erupted, along the road to the Sudanese capital.

Rebels fighting the Sudanese army are advancing on Damazin, about 480 km (300 miles) southeast of the capital, with the aim of putting pressure on the Khartoum government and sparking a popular uprising.
Damazin has a hydroelectricity plant which supplies Khartoum with 80 percent of its power.

On Tuesday, rebel leader Colonel John Garang said southern and northern opposition forces were about 60 km (35 miles) south of the town. Sudan says its front line in the war with rebel forces is about 85 to 100 km (50 to 60 miles) from the city at its closest point.

One traveller reported seeing a helicopter gunship and transport plane flying over the Roseires dam which lies just north of Damazin and one light aircraft which flew high and turned back. He said he thought they were Sudanese aircraft.
But the travellers said there was little tension among Damazin residents.
"It is quiet during the night. We hear some shooting at night but we don't know if its because of Ramadan," the traveller said, referring to the Islamic holy month of fasting.
Another traveller said he also occasionally heard gunfire but that Sudanese troops arriving in the town normally fire into the air as a sign of celebration.
Sudan says Ethiopian and Eritrean troops are fighting the eastern battle and that they are using the rebels as their agents. Both the African countries have denied this.
Sudanese officials said in remarks published on Wednesday that Sudan was ready to defend the strategic Roseires dam.
"We have taken the necessary contingencies to secure the dam," Irrigation and Water resources Minister Yacoub Musa Abu- Shora told the government daily Akhbar al-Youm in Damazin.
